meta.description: Intelligent recipe scaling rules for spices, pan sizes, cooking times, and scaling warnings
sources: America's Test Kitchen - The Science of Good Cooking

spice_scaling.description: Spices and seasonings don't scale linearly. Salt is perceived differently at higher concentrations, and aromatic compounds become overwhelming.

salt.notes: Salt perception is highly non-linear. At 2x recipe, use ~1.5x salt. Taste and adjust.
salt.danger_message: At 4x+ scale, salt can easily become overwhelming. Start with 2x original and taste.

hot_spices.notes: Hot spices compound aggressively. At 2x recipe, use only ~1.4x hot spice.
hot_spices.danger_message: Heat builds quickly! Use half the scaled amount and add more to taste.

aromatic_spices.notes: Aromatic spices can become overpowering. Scale conservatively.

dried_herbs.notes: Dried herbs release flavor over time. For larger batches, reduce cooking time slightly or use less.

fresh_herbs.notes: Fresh herbs scale more linearly than dried, but still slightly reduce for large batches.

garlic_onion.notes: Alliums can become pungent at high concentrations. Scale conservatively for raw applications.

vanilla_extracts.notes: Extracts are concentrated. At 2x recipe, use ~1.6x extract.

leavening.notes: Leavening agents scale nearly linearly but can cause texture issues at extreme scales.
leavening.danger_message: At 3x+ scale, baking may require pan/time adjustments. Consider baking in batches.

acidic_ingredients.notes: Acids can become harsh at higher concentrations. Scale conservatively and adjust to taste.

sweeteners_baking.notes: Sugar scales nearly linearly for baking chemistry, but taste may warrant slight reduction.
sweeteners_baking.context_note: In baking, sugar affects structure. Don't reduce by more than 10% without testing.

pan_sizes.description: Recommended pan sizes based on recipe yield and scaling factor

cookies.0.5: Use standard sheet pan, expect fewer cookies
cookies.2: Two standard sheet pans or one half-sheet pan
cookies.4: Multiple batches recommended (rotate pans for even baking)

cakes_round.1: Use 8-inch or 9-inch round pans (as recipe specifies)
cakes_round.1.5: Use 10-inch round pans or three 8-inch layers
cakes_round.2: Use 10-inch round pans or bake in batches

brownies_bars.2: Use half-sheet pan or two 9x13 pans
brownies_bars.4: Use full sheet pan or bake in multiple batches

casseroles.2: Use two 9x13 dishes or one large roasting pan
casseroles.4: Use multiple 9x13 dishes or commercial-size pan

bread_loaves.4: Use four loaf pans or consider commercial-size

cooking_time_adjustments.description: Cooking times don't scale linearly. Larger batches often need different approaches.

stovetop_liquids.description: Soups, sauces, and liquids on stovetop
stovetop_liquids.scaling_factor: Approximately square root of volume ratio
stovetop_liquids.example: 2x liquid = ~1.4x time to bring to boil
stovetop_liquids.notes: Use wider pot if available to maintain surface area.

stovetop_saute.scaling_note: Don't scale up - work in batches!
stovetop_saute.max_batch: Fill pan no more than one layer deep
stovetop_saute.notes: For 2x recipe, saute in two batches and combine.

oven_baking.notes: Time increases with pan size/depth, not just volume
oven_baking.shallow_items: Cookies, thin bars - time stays similar if spread on more pans
oven_baking.deep_items: Cakes, casseroles - add 25-50% time for doubled depth
oven_baking.temperature_note: May need to reduce temp by 25°F for very large items to prevent burning edges

oven_roasting.meat_rule: Time scales with weight: use meat thermometer, not time
oven_roasting.vegetable_rule: Use multiple pans rather than crowding; time stays similar
oven_roasting.crowding_warning: Overcrowded roasting pans steam instead of roast

slow_cooker.notes: Fill 1/2 to 2/3 full for best results
slow_cooker.scaling_down: May cook faster if less full - check earlier
slow_cooker.scaling_up: Don't exceed 2/3 full; liquid should cover solids

pressure_cooker.description: Instant Pot and pressure cooker recipes
pressure_cooker.notes: Time under pressure stays same for most items
pressure_cooker.max_fill: Never exceed max fill line (usually 2/3 or less)

deep_frying.reason: Adding too much cold food drops oil temperature, causing greasy results
deep_frying.max_batch: No more than fills 1/4 of oil surface
deep_frying.recovery_time: Allow oil to return to temp between batches

cookies.notes: Bake same time per batch. Multiple batches, not longer time.

cake_layers.notes: Use more/larger pans, not deeper pans. Same time if same depth.

cake_deep.notes: Deeper pans need 25% more time. Reduce temp 25°F to prevent burning.

casserole.notes: Slightly longer if deeper. Check internal temp 165°F for safety.

soup_stew.notes: Bring to boil time increases. Simmer time stays similar once hot.

rice_grains.notes: Slight increase. Keep lid on; don't lift to check too often.

pasta_boiling.notes: Same cook time once water re-boils. Use larger pot with more water.

meat_roasting.time_note: Use thermometer! Time varies with thickness, not weight alone.

scaling_warnings.description: Categories and specific items that don't scale well or have special considerations

souffles.warning: Soufflés are extremely temperamental and should not be scaled. Make multiple individual soufflés instead of one larger one.

meringues.warning: Meringues are sensitive to humidity and technique. Scaling up significantly increases failure risk.

custards_flans.warning: Custards set based on temperature gradients. Larger portions may not set properly in the center.

yeast_breads.warning: Large dough batches are difficult to knead and may not rise evenly. Consider making multiple batches.
yeast_breads.tip: For 2x+, use a stand mixer with dough hook, or divide and knead in portions.

candy_confections.warning: Candy making depends on precise temperature control. Larger batches take longer to reach temperature, affecting texture.

emulsions.warning: Emulsion sauces can break when made in large quantities. Make in smaller batches and combine.

deep_fried.warning: Deep frying must be done in small batches regardless of recipe size. Scale refers to total quantity, not batch size.
deep_fried.tip: Fry in batches of 4-6 pieces. Keep finished items warm in 200°F oven.

cheese_sauces.warning: Cheese can become grainy if overheated. Make in smaller batches or use lower heat for large quantities.

minimum_yeast.warning: Below half scale, yeast may not activate properly. Use at least 1/4 tsp active dry yeast.

minimum_eggs.warning: Recipes using 1 egg don't scale down well. Consider using half an egg (beat and measure) or egg substitute.
minimum_eggs.tip: 1 large egg = ~3 tbsp. For half recipe, use 1.5 tbsp beaten egg.

minimum_leavening.warning: Very small amounts of leavening are hard to measure accurately. Use a precision scale.

pan_equivalents.description: Pan size conversions when scaling recipes

9x13_rect.equivalent_to: Two 8-inch rounds (100 sq in) or two 9-inch rounds (127 sq in)

ingredient_behavior.description: How specific ingredients behave when scaled

flour.notes: Flour is structural and scales linearly for chemistry. Measure by weight for accuracy.

eggs.notes: Eggs are structural. For odd numbers, beat egg and measure by volume (1 egg = 3 tbsp).

butter_fat.notes: Fat is structural in baking. Scales linearly but can affect richness at high scales.

liquid.notes: Liquids scale linearly but affect cooking time.

detection_patterns.description: Patterns to detect recipe types for appropriate warnings
